A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the carnitine pathway is a critical regulator of the cellular stress responses and that the activation of this pathway is a key factor in the maintenance of cellular homeostasis and the prevention of aging and neurodegeneration.
the hormesis and vitagenes theory of aging and neurodegeneration is the most promising theory of the aging process, as well as the most promising theory for neurodegenerative disease.

carnitine is a key regulator of mitochondrial function and a major player in the control of cellular homeostasis, which may be a key to the understanding of how cells adapt and survive under stressful conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the carnitine and heat shock response systems are highly interconnected, and that the heat shock response can be activated by carnitine, and that the activation of the heat shock system by carnitine is mediated by hormetic dose responses, and that the carnitines can be used to modulate hormetic dose responses.
carnitine insufficiencies may be critical determinants in aging and neurodegeneration.

the carnitine insufficiency, as a consequence of aging or disease, may lead to mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, which, in turn, may lead to the activation of vitagenes, such as the heat shock response, the antioxidant response and the autophagic response, as a compensatory response.
